decisions.reason: A compact dumper with rotating skip is close to a long-established machinery maker’s existing engineering and market knowledge, so the firm is likely to learn quickly from first-year feedback and improve rather than withdraw it.

An articulated construction dumper fits strongly with core construction-equipment capabilities and customer relationships, which under an absorptive-capacity view makes commercial refinement more likely than exit.

The underground mine rescue vehicle is more niche and demands specialised application knowledge, so withdrawal risk is materially higher, but a German machinery firm with related special-vehicle know-how would still more likely retain it to build experience and partnerships.

A compact telescopic loader is adjacent to the firm’s apparent off-highway machinery base, and although it may require some new integration and market learning, the knowledge overlap is high enough to favour continuation.
